_**Agent (auto-smart)**_

> **Decision:** Which JoRap Notes features earn their keep — keep, demote, or cut — across ~339 notes and the full browse / graph / flashcard / authoring stack?

### White
Known: atomic notes with structured frontmatter (`description`, `key_concept`, `level_1`–`5`, `examples`, `shareable_thought`, `relationships`); wikilinks, backlinks, See also; `/notes/` search/tags; local + global graph (Pixi); Faith/EP flashcards + `/notes/review/` + Anki; Random Duo / random note; Issues, Create Note, OKF/Agent copy; lint/`garden:health`; blog↔notes; section RSS. ~110 notes have `review: true`. Strict wikilink lint is off. Issue counts were dropped from the toolbar for speed.

Unknown without analytics: which pages anyone besides you actually opens (graph, Random Duo, review, Create, OKF, shareable grid). Unknown: how often you run spaced review vs just authoring cards. Checkable later: Cloudflare analytics or server logs by path; your own last-30-days habit for `/notes/review/`, `/notes/graph/`, Random Duo.

### Red
This garden feels like a workshop that grew a museum wing. The atomic note + link core feels alive. The rest — graph filters, duo prompts, shareable grids, level ladders, Create Note — feels like tools built because they were cool, not because something broke without them. Mild dread that “useful” got redefined as “feature-complete digital garden.”

### Black
The fatal risk is **surface sprawl that dilutes the product**. A stranger landing on `/notes/` meets catalog + random pair + search + tags + paths into graph, duo, flashcards, review, issues, create, OKF. That is not one job. Authoring cost is worse: every note pays tax for `level_1`–`5`, four `shareable_thought` lines, typed relationships, and often dormant `cards` with `review: false`. That tax compounds across 339 notes and agent/lint time.

Several lanes look like **second products bolted on**: spaced repetition (Anki already exists), graph analytics (Obsidian/OKF viz), ChatGPT handoff panels (Create/Duo/OKF). If you are not using review weekly and not exporting Anki, the review UI is theater. If graph is opened for screenshots and ego, not navigation, it is jewelry. Random Duo’s path + prompt panel is a clever demo that may never change what you write next.

Keeping everything “because a digital garden should have it” is the yes-man trap. Features you do not exercise still cost layout JS, Pixi, lint rules, skills, and mental model when teaching the garden or hiring an agent.

### Yellow
If the full stack is intentional, JoRap Notes becomes a **rare public PKM that is both readable and drillable**: wiki for browsers, Faith cards for memory, typed relationships for argument structure, graph for “show me the shape,” OKF for agent reuse. That is a portfolio piece and a personal OS, not a blog sidebar.

Shareable thoughts + examples + level ladder turn each note into a teaching object — paste, scene, depth — without rewriting for social. Issues + garden health make a large corpus maintainable instead of rotting. Blog↔notes and site search make the garden feed the public site instead of living in a silo. Random Duo / Create are on-ramps when you are stuck: serendipity and scaffold instead of blank-page guilt. In the best case, nothing here is waste — each lane serves a different mode (read, drill, maintain, hand off to AI) and the combination is the brand.

### Green
1. **Do nothing** — keep shipping notes; let unused URLs stay quiet; no cull until you have path hits or a honest “I haven’t opened X in 90 days” list.
2. **Keep core, demote the rest** — core = atomic notes, wikilinks/backlinks/relationships, `/notes/` browse+search, MOCs, Getting Started, lint/health. Soft-hide or stop linking from main nav: Random Duo, Create, OKF page, global graph (keep local if cheap), shareable grid (keep field, stop featuring). Freeze new flashcard UI work; keep Anki export if you still use Anki.
3. **Cut for real** — delete or `draft`/unpublish Create, Random Duo, Issues-as-public-page (CLI-only), Pixi global graph; strip `level_*` / `shareable_thought` from required shape for new notes; Faith cards stay in frontmatter for Anki only, drop on-site review.

### Outsider
A stranger sees a personal wiki with an unusual YAML template, then a pile of side apps: flashcard trainer, network graph, random two-note toy with ChatGPT prompts, “create note” wizard, export formats. It looks like one person built every Obsidian plugin as a static page. Unclear who the audience is — readers, your future self drilling Faith, or agents eating OKF. The claim “notes garden” does not explain why I need a review session and a duo pathfinder. Weirdest bit: maintenance dashboards and AI scaffolds sitting next to teaching notes as if they were the same product.

### Executor
Tonight: open Cloudflare (or whatever you have) analytics for the last 90 days and list hit counts for `/notes/`, `/notes/graph/`, `/notes/review/`, `/notes/flashcards/`, `/notes/random-duo/`, `/notes/create/`, `/notes/issues/`, `/notes/okf-export/`. Rank by visits. That single list decides the cull conversation — no opinions without numbers.

### Self-review
1. **Strongest block:** Black — the authoring tax + “second product” framing is the real usefulness test.
2. **Biggest blind spot:** No usage data; hats are guessing from architecture, not behavior.
3. **Missed by all blocks:** Whether *you* still personally open review/graph/duo weekly — owner habit beats visitor analytics for a personal garden.

### Blue

## Where the lenses agree
The linked atomic note (frontmatter claim + wikilinks + browse/search + MOCs + health/lint) is the product. Extra surfaces exist; usefulness is not proven uniformly. Faith flashcards are a coherent second lane only if you actually drill or export.

## Where the lenses clash
Yellow wants the full multimodal OS (wiki + drill + graph + agent handoff) as brand. Black/Outsider want fewer public jobs and less per-note tax. Green’s “demote” vs “cut” is the real fork — demote costs almost nothing; cut frees maintenance forever.

## Blind spots
No path analytics in this run. No confirmation of your last review/Anki/graph session. Dormant `cards` on non-Faith notes were noted but not costed.

## The recommendation
Treat notes features as **three tiers, not one pile**: (1) **Keep and invest** — atomic notes, wikilinks/backlinks/relationships, index search/tags, MOCs/Getting Started, garden lint/health, blog↔notes. (2) **Keep if you use weekly, else demote** — on-site review + flashcards gallery (Faith/EP only), Anki export, local graph; global graph and Random Duo stay only if analytics or habit say yes. (3) **Demote from the reader path now** — Create Note, public Issues, OKF marketing page, shareable-thought *grid as a featured UI*, and hard requirements for `level_1`–`5` on every new note (fields can stay optional). Do not mass-delete code this week; stop linking them as equal peers of “read the garden.” Usefulness fails when every feature claims equal status. Re-promote only with evidence.

## The one thing to do first
Pull 90-day path hits for graph, review, flashcards, random-duo, create, issues, and okf-export — then mark each demote or keep on that list before touching layouts.

_**Agent (auto-smart)**_

> **Reframe:** Same cull question — but the notes stack is an **AI-powered garden** (agent authoring, OKF/Agent copy, Create/Duo prompts, lint/voice skills), not a human-only wiki with toys on the side. Does that change keep / demote / cut?

### White
Known from last pass: core wiki + many side surfaces. New fact: several “niche” lanes are **agent I/O**, not reader chrome — OKF flatten, Agent copy, hub cluster copy, Create Note scaffolds, Random Duo ChatGPT prompts, garden-voice/flashcards skills, `lint:garden` as machine-checkable shape. Humans still read notes; AI is how notes get written, linked, audited, and handed off.

Unknown: whether *you* still drive most creation through agents vs typing YAML yourself; whether public visitors use Create/Duo or only you + agents do. Checkable: how often Agent copy / OKF / Create appear in your sessions; whether demoting public links breaks agent workflows that hit URLs.

### Red
Relief, a bit. The stack felt like feature tourism; as an AI workbench it feels less accidental. Still annoyed if the *reader* path has to wear the workbench. Gut: don’t kill the AI rails — hide them from tourists.

### Black
AI-powered does **not** make every feature useful. It reframes waste: useless = **AI surface that neither you nor agents actually call**. Create/Duo/OKF that sit unused are still theater — now “AI theater.” Worse failure mode: optimizing the garden for agents until notes read like schema for models (level ladders, four shareables, typed edges) while humans bounce. And AI does not excuse public sprawl: a visitor still meets graph + duo + create + review as peer products. Powering authoring with AI strengthens **author/agent tooling**; it does not automatically strengthen **on-site review, Pixi graph analytics, or shareable grids** unless those feed the AI loop or your drill habit.

### Yellow
If AI is the engine, the “second products” become **ports**: OKF = context pack; Agent copy = one-shot paste; Create = cold-start; Duo = serendipity prompt; Issues + lint = machine-readable health; structured frontmatter = reliable extraction. Faith cards stay a human drill lane, but the same YAML is clean for agents. The brand sharpens: not “another digital garden,” but a garden **built to be written and queried with AI** without leaving Hugo. Investing in those rails compounds every future note; cutting them to look minimal is cutting your co-author’s hands.

### Green
1. **Do nothing on code** — keep AI surfaces; change only how you talk about the garden (docs: “reader path” vs “agent path”).
2. **Split the IA** — one clear reader spine (browse, note, MOC, optional Faith review); tuck Create / OKF / Issues / Duo / heavy graph under “Tools” or author docs. Same features, different status.
3. **Cut only confirmed orphans** — if analytics *and* your agent habits never touch a surface for 90 days, remove it; do not cut OKF/Agent copy on vibes alone now that AI is the premise.

### Outsider
“AI powers my notes” explains the weird YAML and export buttons. It still looks odd if the homepage of the garden doesn’t say that. A stranger thinks: either this is a personal wiki with too many gadgets, or it’s an AI-assisted knowledge base that forgot to label the workshop door. Clearest fix in their head: two doors — Read the garden / Work the garden (AI).

### Executor
Update Getting Started (or Reading the Garden) with a two-lane map: **Read** vs **AI/tools** — three bullets each, linking Create, OKF, Agent copy, Issues under tools. No code deletion today.

### Self-review
1. **Strongest:** Yellow’s “ports not toys” — correctly flips OKF/Create/Agent copy from demote-default to keep-default.
2. **Blind spot:** Still no proof you *use* those ports weekly.
3. **Missed earlier:** Treating AI authoring as load-bearing changes **priority of demotion**, not the need for a reader/agent split.

### Blue

## Where the lenses agree
AI as the powering force **rescues author/agent tooling** (OKF, Agent copy, Create, lint/shape, structured frontmatter) from last pass’s “demote by default.” It does **not** automatically rescue reader-facing extras (global graph flex, Random Duo as peer nav, shareable grid as hero UI, on-site SRS) without habit or hits.

## Where the lenses clash
Yellow: invest in the AI workbench as brand. Black: AI can still produce theater and human-hostile schema. Outsider wants labeling more than deletion.

## Blind spots
Usage of Agent copy / OKF / Create in real sessions still unmeasured. Whether Faith review is AI-adjacent or purely human drill.

## The recommendation
**Yes — opinions change for the tool lane; mostly not for the reader lane.** Reclassify: **Keep and treat as first-class for AI** — atomic shape, wikilinks/relationships, OKF, Agent/hub copy, Create, garden lint/health, voice skills. **Still demote from the main reader path** (not necessarily delete) — Create/OKF/Issues/Duo/heavy graph as peer destinations on `/notes/`. **Still conditional** — on-site review, Anki, local graph: keep if you use them; AI doesn’t invent that habit. Last pass’s “demote Create/OKF now” was wrong under an AI-powered premise; the split-IA move is the corrected call.

## The one thing to do first
Document the two-lane map (Read vs AI/tools) on Getting Started / Reading the Garden so the stack matches the premise — then run the 90-day path check only to find true orphans, not to justify cutting the AI ports.
